findings.title: Federation requests follow redirects to plain http, so an https-only check is bypassed
stellar.toml fetch follows redirects to plain HTTP, so the HTTPS-only default can be downgraded
SEP-10 threshold check fails open when threshold is undefined, null or NaN
Security settings live in one process-wide object, so one Server or caller changes allowHttp for all tenants
Unbounded Horizon Date header sets transaction maxTime via fetchTimebounds
BadResponseError branch in submitTransaction is unreachable for Horizon HTTP errors
resolveAddress sends a full name*domain address to a server for a different domain
findings.evidence: federation_server.ts:183 `const url = this.serverURL.query({ type: "name", q: stellarAddress });`

findings.title: HTTP error branch never reaches BadResponseError, so error status is lost
Process-wide X-App-Name interceptor leaks one Server's headers into every other Server's requests
forAccount does not validate the account ID format before building the payments query
Native buying()/selling() leaves the previous asset's code and issuer in the offers query
ledger() accepts any sequence string or number without validation
setTimeout stores NaN or negative values, which break every stellar.toml and federation request
forAccount on OfferCallBuilder accepts any string as an account ID
sponsor() on OfferCallBuilder sets an unvalidated sponsor ID as a query value
forLedger accepts any string sequence and places it unvalidated in the Horizon path
forTransaction accepts any string and places it unvalidated in the Horizon path
Unguarded JSON.parse in stream listener drops malformed Horizon messages without reporting them
Federation requests have no timeout by default (Config timeout 0 means unlimited)
Process-wide SERVER_TIME_MAP grows without bound from response-driven hostnames
stellar.toml resolve has no time bound by default, so a stalled host hangs the caller
submitTransaction rejects after a successful send when the result XDR fails to decode
Rejected or timed-out submission leaves the outcome ambiguous and invites a paying retry
Config.setAllowHttp stores any value without a runtime boolean check
Zero-weight (removed) account signers pass SEP-10 threshold check when threshold is 0
Federation address domain is used unvalidated to build a server-side stellar.toml fetch (SSRF)
Link follow does not keep the request on HTTPS: an http:// href from a Horizon response is fetched in plaintext
Collection next/prev pagination follows an absolute host from the Horizon response without checking it against the configured server
HAL pagination and link follow requests to any absolute host in a Horizon response
submitTransaction gives no hash-based reconciliation after a timed-out or 504 submit, so callers that retry pay twice
Global allowHttp switch makes stellar.toml and federation lookups plain HTTP, enabling account redirection
